name: Kössen
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village by Walchsee and the wild Kaiser, featuring a watersports paradise and a nature reserve.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kössen is a vibrant market town in northeastern Tyrol and the centerpiece of the Kaiserwinkl holiday region. Situated at an altitude of 589 metres in a sunny valley basin along the Großache river, the municipality directly borders Bavaria's Chiemgau district. Framed by the rugged limestone cliffs of the Zahmer Kaiser range to the south and the rolling Chiemgau Alps to the north, Kössen and its roughly 4,500 residents boast an alluring alpine setting. Renowned internationally as a premier hotspot for paragliders and hang gliders taking off from the Unterberg, the town also charms hikers, outdoor athletes, and families seeking untouched nature such as the Entenlochklamm gorge.

History

The area surrounding Kössen has been inhabited since prehistoric times, with the parish first formally documented around 1180 under the name Chossen. Given its strategic border location, the settlement functioned for centuries as an important trading hub for salt, timber, and iron along alpine bridle paths connecting Tyrol and Bavaria. Historic smugglers' tracks traversed the dramatic Entenlochklamm gorge and the pass at Klobenstein. The commanding parish church of St. Peter and Paul was constructed in baroque splendor between 1719 and 1722 by master builder Georg Wech. In the 1970s, Kössen earned worldwide acclaim when it hosted the first Hang Gliding World Championship on the Unterberg in 1975, establishing the town as a cradle of foot-launched flight.

Getting There

Kössen is easily reached from both Austria and Germany. By car from within Austria, take the A12 Inntal Autobahn to exit Kufstein-Süd, continuing via Niederndorf and Walchsee. Coming from Bavaria, the toll-free route runs along the German A8 motorway via Bernau am Chiemsee and through Reit im Winkl straight into the Kaiserwinkl basin. Train travelers can alight at main stations in Kufstein or St. Johann in Tirol, where regular regional buses operated by the VVT connect directly to the center of Kössen.

Tips

A premier outdoor highlight is walking the historic Smugglers' Trail through the Entenlochklamm gorge. This impressive trail features two suspension footbridges spanning over 30 metres above the Großache river, leading to the pilgrimage shrine of Maria Klobenstein with its legendary split rock. Flight enthusiasts can enjoy world-class thermals and tandem paragliding from the Unterberghorn, while in winter the Hochkössen ski area provides 22 kilometres of family-friendly slopes. Cross-country skiers can access the Kaiserwinkl network comprising over 120 kilometres of groomed tracks, and Lake Walchsee nearby offers refreshing summer swimming.
